newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago NBD seeks to offer equity.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago NBD seeks to offer equity.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp said Wednesday it applied to the Federal Reserve Board for permission to distribute and underwrite equity securities, after losing out on nine deals this year because it could not offer an equity component.
F. Gerald Byrne, chairman of First Chicago Capital Markets, a unit of First Chicago, said the unit needs the ability to underwrite warrants and preferred stock as part of high-yield debt packages.
"There is an increasing percentage of high-yield business that is done with a warrant in it," Byrne said in a telephone interview.

So far in 1997, First Chicago had to pass on four high-yield offerings because it could not underwrite a warrant that was part of the deal, Byrne said. First Chicago was also unable to participate in five deals for a utility client because the deals would have included preffered stock, he said. Both warrants and preferred stock are considered equity.
Byrne said First Chicago planned to underwrite equity as a supplement to its alliance with Robert W. Baird & Co Inc, but would not become a full-service equity player.
"We're not going to build, make the investment to become a full-service equity house," Byrne said. He added that First Chicago was not currently contemplating buying an equity underwriting firm.
The approval process from the Federal Reserve would take at least until August, Byrne said.
First Chicago Capital markets currently has authority to underwrite and distribute government securities, municipal bonds, commercial paper, asset-backed securities and corporate debt.
First Chicago shares were up 13/16 to 63-15/16 Wednesday.
